claims.text: The initial TaNbHfZrTi-based alloy is a largely homogeneous, disordered solid solution.
Substituting approximately 5% of one constituent with W introduces chemical pressure.
The W substitution causes subtle changes in lattice parameters.
W-induced chemical pressure shifts the alloy's electronic band structure.
The band-structure shift alters the electronic density of states near the Fermi level.
A change in the density of states near the Fermi level modulates superconducting electron-pairing interactions.
The modified pairing interactions produce a measurable change in superconducting transition temperature relative to the baseline alloy.
The modified pairing interactions produce an altered superconducting gap relative to the baseline alloy.
Correlated changes in lattice parameters, Fermi-level density of states, Tc, and superconducting gap would support the proposed electronic mechanism.
At approximately 5% W substitution, chemical pressure can be introduced without fundamentally changing the overall chemical disorder or inducing new phases.
The proposed effect is expected to be significant only for minor W additions around 5%.
Larger W substitutions may create additional extrinsic disorder or secondary phases.
W-induced disorder or impurity scattering could affect superconductivity independently of band-structure changes.
A controlled comparison uses a W-free TaNbHfZrTi baseline and a 5% W-substituted sample synthesized under identical processing conditions.
Absence of a statistically significant density-of-states shift, or equivalence of Tc and gap within experimental uncertainty, is designated as falsifying the hypothesis.
